results.evidence: dist_km renders as 'Approach (one way)'; 1.6 km (~1.0 mi) is the Smithbrook Trail from the trailhead to Union Gap, which is exactly where the row's own approach text ends the approach ('climbs about 1 mile to the PCT junction at Union Gap, the start of the scramble route'). The Forest Service lists Smithbrook Trail at 0.9 mi and other sources say roughly one mile to the PCT junction, so dist_km is a different quantity (approach to the scramble start) from the itinerary's car-to-car round trip, not a conflicting value. Whether the 5.4 mi round trip itself is right is recorded separately as a discovered, unresolved item.

results.fact: Total gain stated as 2,400 ft in one place, 1,696 ft everywhere else
results.correct_value: about 1,700 ft of gain (trailhead 4,000 ft to summit 5,696 ft; gain_ft 1696 stays)
results.evidence: The Forest Service Smithbrook Trailhead page gives the trailhead elevation as 4,000 ft; WTA gives Union Peak's high point as 5,696 ft, so a straight up-and-back is ~1,700 ft. Komoot independently puts Union Gap at ~4,626 ft with ~620 ft of gain on the Smithbrook Trail, consistent with a ~4,000 ft trailhead. One older source puts the trailhead at 3,800 ft (~1,900 ft gain); no source supports 2,400 ft, and gain_ft, loss_ft, the day's gainFt/lossFt and both end waypoints all say 1,696.

results.fact: Car-to-car distance: waypoint distMi (summit 2.7 mi one way) and itinerary 5.4 mi round trip look too long for the geometry
results.evidence: The Smithbrook Trail to Union Gap is 0.9 mi per the Forest Service (~1 mi elsewhere; Komoot says 2.09 km/1.3 mi, matching the waypoint's 1.3), and the summit pin is only ~0.33 mi straight-line from the Union Gap pin, so 1.4 mi of off-trail travel from the gap (waypoints 1.3 -> 2.7) and a 5.4 mi round trip look inflated; a ~3-3.5 mi round trip seems more likely. No two sources give a summer car-to-car figure for Union Peak alone (published totals include the 2.8 mi winter road walk and/or Jove Peak), so nothing was changed.

results.fact: Parking pass: access.fees / access.passRequired say no Northwest Forest Pass, while permit, the Trailhead waypoint note and the Smithbrook bivy entry say one is required
results.evidence: The current Forest Service Smithbrook Trailhead page says no fees are required, and the Smithbrook Trailhead is not on the Region 6 list of day-use-fee sites. WTA and SummitPost-derived descriptions still say a Northwest Forest Pass is required there. The official sources point to 'no pass', but they are both from one agency and conflict with widely used hiking pages, and the same claim sits on shared bivy text used across neighbouring routes, so it was left for a catalog-wide decision rather than patched on one route.
